newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire Water names Kevin Bond CEO.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire Water names Kevin Bond CEO.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Yorkshire Water Plc said Kevin Bond, currently chairman of its water services unit, had been appointed group chief executive.
Bond, who joined the company in April 1996, will continue as chairman of the services unit, which runs the company's regulated water and sewage businesses.
He will be replaced in his post as managing director of water services by Jonson Cox, currently chairman and managing director of Yorkshire's environmental unit.
Cox will take up his new post in April 1997, Yorkshire Water said.
Yorkshire Water said it was seeking a replacement managing director for its environmental unit.
Bond's appointment "confirms our confidence in his ability to help the company progress strongly in the future," chairman Brandon Gough said in a statement.

Gough took over as chairman in April 1996. Bond also joined the company then after a management shake-up and departures following Yorkshire's heavily criticised handling of a drought during the summer of 1995.
Sir Gordon Jones retired as chairman in April 1996 and managing director Trevor Newton, who gained notoriety for not being economical with baths as he claimed, left the company in May 1996.
Since Newton's departure, Yorkshire has had no group managing director and the chief executive position replaces that vacancy, a company spokeswoman said.
